text: Ignorance more frequently begets confidence than does knowledge.
author: Charles Darwin

text: The world of ideas is large and cannot be exhausted.
author: Anton Chekhov

text: Our knowledge is amazing; our ignorance even more so.
author: Dana Meadows

text: Quotation is a serviceable substitute for wit.
author: Oscar Wilde

text: Good luck will be the residue of good design.
author: David Mamet

text:
Design has to work.
Art does not.
author: Donald Judd

text: It is impossible to be too clear.
author: Dylan Thomas

text: The chains that bind mankind are made of office paperwork.
author: Franz Kafka

text: Morality is temporary. Wisdom is permanent.
author: Hunter S. Thompsons

text: If we possess our why of life we can put up with almost any how.
author: Friedrich Nietzsche

text: We talk far too much. We should talk less and draw more.
author: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe

text: Efforts to solve a problem must be preceded by efforts to understand it.
author: Herbert Simon

text: I can calculate the motions of heavenly bodies, but not the madness of people.
author: Isaac Newton

text: Striving to better, oft we mar what’s well.
author: William Shakespeare

text: I like to be on the edge of the possible.
author: Jørn Utzon

text: If a thing is worth doing, it’s worth doing badly.
author: G. K. Chesterton

text: It is not the voice that commands the story: it is the ear.
author: Italo Calvino
